steps.title: Streak yeast on YEPD plates
steps.instruction: Streak a glycerol stock of Saccharomyces cerevisiae VL6‑48N onto a YEPD/agar plate and incubate overnight at 30 °C.

steps.title: Prepare DNA fragments for TAR
steps.instruction: Generate the dsDNA break and HDR fragments for TAR mutagenesis, quantify them, and mix at appropriate molar ratios.

substeps.instruction: Digest >1 µg of the HCoV‑OC43‑YCpBAC plasmid with a chosen restriction endonuclease to create a dsDNA break.
Generate the HDR fragment by PCR or restriction digestion, ensuring ~50 bp homology on each side of the intended mutation.

Determine concentration (ng/µL), length (bp), and pmol of each fragment; calculate the volume needed for a 15:1 mutagenesis‑to‑vector molar ratio (example: 444 ng YCpBAC in 5.41 µL and 405 ng HDR fragment in 7.23 µL).
Combine all fragments in ≤50 µL total volume, using ~100 ng YCpBAC fragment and at least a 5‑fold molar excess of each non‑YCpBAC fragment; keep YCpBAC ≤200 ng (or ~10 ng if PCR‑amplified).
Prepare a “vector‑only” control containing the same amount of YCpBAC fragment.
Store the assembled DNA mixture at –20 °C until use.

steps.title: Inoculate overnight yeast cultures
steps.instruction: Start 2–3 independent overnight cultures of VL6‑48N in YEPD medium.

substeps.instruction: Inoculate 50 mL YEPD medium with small‑to‑medium isolated colonies (one culture per colony) in 250 mL Erlenmeyer flasks.
Incubate at 30 °C with vigorous shaking (120 rpm) overnight.

steps.title: Prepare yeast spheroplasts
steps.instruction: Convert overnight yeast cells to spheroplasts and wash them for transformation.

substeps.instruction: Dilute 50 µL of each overnight culture with 450 µL sterile water (1:10 dilution). Count cells using a hemocytometer; aim for 2–5 × 10⁷ cells mL⁻¹.
If the diluted culture is 5 × 10⁷ cells mL⁻¹, dilute to 5 × 10⁶ cells mL⁻¹ in 50 mL YEPD and incubate at 30 °C with shaking until the density reaches 2–5 × 10⁷ cells mL⁻¹ (≈4 h).
Pellet cells at 3,000 × g for 5 min at 4 °C; discard supernatant.
Warm the required number of 15 mL tubes of SORB‑URA/agar overlay medium to 55 °C.
Resuspend the pellet in sterile water up to 50 mL, vortex, then pellet again at 3,000 × g for 5 min, discard supernatant.
Resuspend in 1 M sorbitol up to 50 mL, vortex, pellet at 3,000 × g for 5 min, discard supernatant.
Add 20 mL SPE solution, vortex, then add 160 µL 10 mg mL⁻¹ zymolyase (20T) and 40 µL β‑mercaptoethanol solution; mix and incubate at 30 °C with gentle shaking (40 rpm) for 20 min.
Check that the overlay medium is melted; if not, microwave in 15‑s intervals with vortexing, keep at 55 °C, and bring plates to room temperature.

Assess spheroplasting: mix 10 µL spheroplast suspension with 90 µL 1 M sorbitol (intact control) and separately with 90 µL 2 % SDS (lysis control). View under phase‑contrast microscopy; proceed when most cells lyse in SDS.
Add 1 M sorbitol up to ~30 mL to dilute zymolyase, pellet spheroplasts at 700 × g for 10 min at 4 °C, discard supernatant.
Wash twice with ~50 mL 1 M sorbitol each: resuspend, pellet at 700 × g for 10 min at 4 °C, discard supernatant.
Resuspend the final spheroplast pellet in 2 mL STC solution (enough for ten transformations). Use within 1 h at room temperature.

steps.title: Transform spheroplasts with DNA
steps.instruction: Introduce the YCpBAC and mutagenesis fragments into yeast spheroplasts by PEG‑mediated transformation.

substeps.instruction: In a 1.5 mL tube, combine 200 µL spheroplast suspension with the DNA mixture prepared in step 2 (or YCpBAC alone for the vector‑only control). Incubate at room temperature for 10 min. Optionally add denatured salmon sperm DNA to bring total DNA to 5 µg.
Add 900 µL PEG solution, invert gently to mix, and incubate at room temperature for 20 min.
Pellet spheroplasts at 700 × g for 5 min in a microcentrifuge; carefully remove supernatant without disturbing the pellet.
Resuspend the pellet in 800 µL SOS solution, then incubate at 30 °C for 30 min without shaking.
Transfer the SOS suspension into a 15 mL tube containing melted SORB‑URA/agar overlay medium, invert twice, and immediately pour the mixture onto pre‑warmed SORB‑URA/agar plates.
Incubate plates at 30 °C for 4–6 days (or at room temperature for slower growth) until colonies appear.

steps.title: Patch colonies onto SD‑URA plates
steps.instruction: Transfer yeast transformant colonies to selective SD‑URA medium for further analysis.

substeps.instruction: Pick at least 23 colonies from each transformation plate (excluding vector‑only plates) and patch each onto a separate SD‑URA/agar plate; number the patches.
Incubate the SD‑URA plates at 30 °C for 1–2 days.

steps.title: Screen colonies by yeast PCR
steps.instruction: Perform colony PCR to identify correct TAR recombinants.

substeps.instruction: Thaw CPZ solution, ThermoPol buffer, dNTPs, and primers on ice.
Dispense 20 µL CPZ solution into each well of a 96‑well PCR plate (use 24 wells per transformation). Keep the plate on ice.
Transfer a small visible amount of each patched colony into the corresponding well; the suspension should be lightly turbid.
Seal the plate and incubate at 37 °C for 20 min to lyse cells; store on ice or at –20 °C.

Prepare a 25 µL PCR master mix per reaction: 2.5 µL 10× ThermoPol Buffer, 0.75 µL 10 mM dNTPs, 0.125 µL 100 µM forward primer, 0.125 µL 100 µM reverse primer, 0.125 µL Taq polymerase, 18.875 µL nuclease‑free water.
In a new 96‑well plate, add 22.5 µL master mix plus 2.5 µL lysate to each well (include a negative control with CPZ only).
Run PCR: 95 °C 3 min; 35 cycles of 95 °C 15 s, 50–68 °C 20 s (primer‑dependent), 68 °C 1 min kb⁻¹; final 68 °C 3 min; hold 10 °C.
Prepare a 1.8 % agarose gel in 1× TAE, load 5 µL 6× loading dye per PCR sample, and run at 85 V for 45 min.
Stain the gel in 1× TAE containing 0.5 µg mL⁻¹ ethidium bromide for 20 min with gentle rocking at room temperature.
Image the gel (e.g., ChemiDoc MP) and identify positive clones.
For each positive clone, add 5 mL SD‑URA medium to a 15 mL tube containing the corresponding patched yeast and incubate at 30 °C overnight with vigorous shaking.

steps.title: Isolate yeast DNA and transform bacteria
steps.instruction: Extract circular YCpBAC plasmid DNA from yeast and electroporate into Stbl3 E. coli.

substeps.instruction: Prepare a glycerol stock of each overnight yeast culture: mix 750 µL culture with 250 µL 50 % glycerol and store at –80 °C.
Pellet the remaining culture at 3,000 × g for 10 min at 4 °C; discard supernatant.
Resuspend the pellet in 2 mL 1 M sorbitol, vortex, then pellet at 3,000 × g for 5 min at 4 °C; discard supernatant.
Add 1.5 mL SPE solution, vortex, then add 12 µL 10 mg mL⁻¹ zymolyase and 3 µL β‑mercaptoethanol; transfer to a 1.5 mL tube and incubate at 37 °C for 30 min.
Pellet spheroplasts at 700 × g for 5 min; discard supernatant.
Add 600 µL QIAGEN cell‑lysis solution, mix gently.
Add 200 µL QIAGEN protein‑precipitation solution, invert to mix, and incubate on ice for 5 min.
Centrifuge at 16,000 × g for 3 min at 4 °C; discard supernatant.
Transfer the cleared lysate to a new tube, add 600 µL isopropanol, and invert 50 times.
Pellet nucleic acids at 16,000 × g for 5 min at 4 °C; discard supernatant.
Wash the pellet with 500 µL 70 % ethanol, invert, then centrifuge again at 16,000 × g for 5 min at 4 °C.
Discard ethanol, briefly aspirate residual liquid (do not overdry), and resuspend the pellet in 100 µL DNA hydration solution; flick to mix.
Add 1.5 µL RNase A, mix, and incubate at 37 °C for 15–60 min (optional 65 °C for up to 1 h).
Measure DNA concentration (spectrophotometer); typical yield >400 ng µL⁻¹.
Thaw electrocompetent Stbl3 E. coli on ice and chill electroporation cuvettes (0.2 cm gap).
Mix 60 µL cells with 10 µL yeast DNA, incubate on ice ≥5 min.
Transfer the mixture to the chilled cuvette and electroporate at 2.5 kV, 25 µF, 200 Ω.
Immediately add 60 µL LB medium, transfer to a 1.5 mL tube, and recover at 37 °C for 1 h with shaking.
Plate the entire recovery on LB/agar containing 17.5 µg mL⁻¹ chloramphenicol; incubate at 37 °C for 1–2 days (expect ≤5 colonies per reaction).

steps.title: Midiprep plasmids for sequencing
steps.instruction: Purify YCpBAC plasmid DNA from bacterial transformants for sequencing and downstream rescue.

substeps.instruction: Pick a single colony from the chloramphenicol plate and inoculate 5 mL LB/chloramphenicol starter culture; grow 37 °C for 6–8 h.
Add 200 µL starter to 100 mL LB/chloramphenicol and incubate overnight at 37 °C with shaking.
Make a glycerol stock of the overnight culture (750 µL culture + 250 µL 50 % glycerol) and store at –80 °C.

Perform a QIAfilter Plasmid Midiprep according to the manufacturer’s protocol, modifying as follows: double the volumes of buffers P1, P2, and P3; increase elution/precipitation volumes; warm buffer QF to 65 °C before use.
Resuspend the DNA pellet in 100 µL Buffer EB; avoid overdrying.
Measure DNA concentration (spectrophotometer); typical >100 ng µL⁻¹.
Submit the plasmid DNA for whole‑plasmid (e.g., Plasmidsaurus) sequencing to verify the absence of unwanted mutations.
For next‑day virus rescue, coat each well of a 6‑well plate with 2 mL of 5 µg mL⁻¹ poly‑L‑lysine (diluted from 1 mg mL⁻¹ stock) for 15 min, then aspirate.
Count HEK‑293T cells with trypan blue, and seed them at 2.5 × 10⁶ cells mL⁻¹ into the coated wells so that they reach 70–80 % confluency the following day.

steps.title: Transfect 293T cells with plasmids
steps.instruction: Introduce the YCpBAC and N‑expressing plasmids into 293T cells to initiate virus rescue.

substeps.instruction: On the day before rescue, seed the poly‑L‑lysine‑coated 6‑well plate with 293T cells as described in the previous step.

Prepare the DNA transfection mixture in Opti‑MEM I: combine 0.9–3.6 µg HCoV‑OC43‑YCpBAC with 0.1–0.4 µg OC43‑N plasmid (pGBW‑m4134906) and bring the volume to ≤100 µL. Prepare a negative‑control mixture with an equivalent amount of unrelated plasmid DNA.
Prepare PEI‑MAX solution: add 3 µL of 1 mg mL⁻¹ PEI per µg of total DNA in Opti‑MEM I, adjusting the final volume to ≤100 µL.
Combine the DNA solution with the PEI‑MAX solution, mix gently, and incubate at room temperature for 15–20 min to allow complex formation.
During the incubation, replace the growth medium on the 293T cells with 1.3 mL Opti‑MEM I per well.
Add the transfection complexes dropwise to the cells, mixing gently.
Incubate the transfected cells at 37 °C, 5 % CO₂ for 2–4 days.

steps.title: Co‑culture with BHK‑21 and passage virus
steps.instruction: Rescue recombinant HCoV‑OC43 by co‑culturing transfected 293T cells with BHK‑21 cells and perform serial passages.

substeps.instruction: Remove medium from the transfected 293T cells, wash gently with PBS, and detach them with 0.25 mL trypsin/EDTA.
Resuspend the 293T cells in 0.75 mL DMEM + 2.5 % FBS + Pen/Strep + L‑glutamine and seed into a 10 cm dish.
Add ~1 × 10⁶ BHK‑21 cells (in DMEM + 2.5 % FBS + Pen/Strep + L‑glutamine) to the same dish, bringing the total volume to 10 mL.
Incubate the co‑culture at 37 °C, 5 % CO₂ for 4–6 days until cytopathic effect (CPE) is evident.
When CPE covers the monolayer, collect the supernatant and centrifuge at 500 × g for 5 min; keep the clarified supernatant as passage 1 and store at –80 °C.

Inoculate a near‑confluent 175 cm² flask of BHK‑21 cells with 2.5 mL passage 1 supernatant diluted in 7.5 mL DMEM (MOI ≈ 0.1 if titer known). Incubate at 37 °C for 1 h with gentle rocking every 15 min.
Replace the inoculum with 25 mL DMEM + 1 % FBS + Pen/Strep + L‑glutamine and incubate 2–3 days at 37 °C, 5 % CO₂ until complete CPE.
Collect the supernatant, centrifuge 500 × g for 5 min, and store as passage 2 (–80 °C).
Determine virus titer by TCID₅₀ assay.
Infect two fresh 175 cm² flasks of BHK‑21 cells with passage 2 at MOI 0.1 (up to 10 mL total volume per flask). Incubate 37 °C for 1 h with rocking.
Replace inoculum with 25 mL DMEM + 1 % FBS + Pen/Strep + L‑glutamine and incubate 2–3 days until CPE.
Collect the final supernatant, centrifuge 500 × g for 5 min, pool the clarified supernatant (passage 3), aliquot 0.5–1 mL, and store at –80 °C as the working virus stock.
